sentences.en: Say kids, what time is it?
sentences.zh: 嘿，孩子们，现在是什么时间？

sentences.en: If your parents or grandparents grew up in the United States in the 1950s,
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母或祖父母是在20世纪50年代的美国长大的，

sentences.en: there's a decent chance that you have heard them sing this song.
sentences.zh: 那么你很有可能听过他们唱这首歌。

sentences.en: And if you're the right age, you can probably sing it yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你年纪刚好，你可能自己也会唱。

sentences.en: In fact, if you're a boomer, it might be stuck in your head right now.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你是婴儿潮一代，这首歌现在可能正萦绕在你的脑海里。

sentences.en: In which case, I am sorry.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: It's time to start the show.
For those who don't know, this nearly atonal chanting is the theme song
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人，这段近乎无调的吟唱是

sentences.en: to one of the very first children's television programs,
sentences.zh: 最早的儿童电视节目之一的主题曲，

sentences.en: Best reporter and longtime 99PI contributor, David Weinberg.
sentences.zh: 这是最棒的记者兼《99%隐形》的长期撰稿人大卫·温伯格。

sentences.en: The Howdy Doody Show is one of those pieces of 1950s ephemera,
sentences.zh: 《豪迪·杜迪秀》是20世纪50年代的那些昙花一现的事物之一，

sentences.en: like the hula hoop, that has come to symbolize mid-century American childhood.
sentences.zh: 就像呼啦圈一样，已经成为中世纪美国童年的象征。

sentences.en: For over a decade, every weeknight at 5 p.m.,
kids all across the country would sit down in front of their parents' tiny television
sentences.zh: 全国各地的孩子们都会坐在父母那台小小的电视机前，

sentences.en: and take in the Wild West adventures of Buffalo Bob and his marionette puppet sidekick,
sentences.zh: 观看“水牛鲍勃”和他的木偶搭档的狂野西部冒险故事，
那个木偶就是豪迪·杜迪。

sentences.en: What do you think we ought to do?
Well, I don't know, Mr. Smith, but I guess everybody likes movies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道，史密斯先生，但我猜大家都喜欢看电影。

sentences.en: At the time, there wasn't anything quite like it.
sentences.zh: 在当时，还没有什么节目能与之相比。

sentences.en: Imagine a singing cowboy performing a puppet show for your birthday,
sentences.zh: 想象一下，一位唱歌的牛仔在你的生日派对上表演木偶戏，
而且每周有五天晚上都是如此。

sentences.en: And now imagine nearly every other kid in America enjoying the same party at the same time.
sentences.zh: 现在再想象一下，美国几乎所有其他孩子都在同一时间享受着同样的派对。

sentences.en: For a lot of children, it was their first encounter with the concept of a TV star.
sentences.zh: 对许多孩子来说，这是他们第一次接触到“电视明星”这个概念。

sentences.en: Which is why Bert Dubrow can remember exactly where he was when he first heard the rumor.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么伯特·杜布罗能清楚地记得他第一次听到那个传闻时自己在哪里。

sentences.en: I was out on a playground in 5th or 6th grade, Trinity School in New Rochelle, New York.
sentences.zh: 我在五年级或六年级时，在纽约新罗谢尔的三一学校操场上。

sentences.en: And some kid said that Buffalo Bob bought a liquor store in New Rochelle.
sentences.zh: 有个孩子说“水牛鲍勃”在新罗谢尔买了一家酒铺。

sentences.en: Now, that would be like saying Mr. Rogers owned a liquor store.
sentences.zh: 这就像是说罗杰斯先生拥有一家酒铺一样。

sentences.en: And at the time, Bert loved all things TV, especially live TV, and especially Howdy Doody.
sentences.zh: 当时，伯特热爱电视上的一切，尤其是直播电视，尤其是《豪迪·杜迪》。

sentences.en: So when he heard this rumor that the show's host, Buffalo Bob, was selling liquor in New Rochelle,
sentences.zh: 所以当他听到这个传闻，说节目主持人“水牛鲍勃”在新罗谢尔卖酒时，

sentences.en: he couldn't stop thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 他满脑子想的都是这件事。

sentences.en: And I literally found the route from the south end to the north end.
sentences.zh: 我真的找到了从南端到北端的路线。

sentences.en: And I did not tell my parents.
sentences.zh: 而且我没有告诉我的父母。

sentences.en: And I got in the M bus, and I got off, and there was big signs that said liquors.
sentences.zh: 我上了M路公交车，下车后，看到写着“酒类”的大招牌。

sentences.en: Ten years old, I walked into the liquor store.
sentences.zh: 十岁的我走进了那家酒铺。

sentences.en: My chin came up to the counter.
sentences.zh: 我的下巴刚好够到柜台。

sentences.en: And I said, excuse me, is Buffalo Bob here?
sentences.zh: 我说，请问，水牛鲍勃在这里吗？

sentences.en: And there was a man behind the counter who was wearing a Czech shirt, black horn-rimmed glasses,
sentences.zh: 柜台后面有一个穿着捷克衬衫、戴着黑色粗框眼镜的男人，

sentences.en: Well, that made no sense to me, because he didn't look like Buffalo Bob.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对我来说毫无意义，因为他看起来不像水牛鲍勃。

sentences.en: He didn't, did that second sound like Buffalo Bob.
sentences.zh: 他不像，那一秒听起来也不像水牛鲍勃。

sentences.en: And he reached down below the counter, and he pulled out a colored picture, that one right over there, in the red frame,
sentences.zh: 他伸手到柜台下面，拿出一张彩色照片，就是那边红框里的那张，

sentences.en: And as he was talking, he started to sound like Buffalo Bob.
sentences.zh: 当他说话时，他的声音开始变得像水牛鲍勃了。

sentences.en: That's when Burt realized that this was really happening.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，伯特意识到这一切都是真的。

sentences.en: He was standing in front of his hero, the actual living, breathing Buffalo Bob, selling liquor.
sentences.zh: 他正站在他的英雄面前，那个活生生的、真实的水牛鲍勃，正在卖酒。

sentences.en: My parents were ready to kill me.
sentences.zh: 我的父母当时简直想杀了我。

sentences.en: So I was at Buffalo Bob's liquor store.
sentences.zh: 我去水牛鲍勃的酒铺了。

sentences.en: Well, they thought I was smoking something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们以为我抽了什么东西。

sentences.en: But every day, or many days after that, I went.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，每天，或者很多天，我都去了。

sentences.en: It reached a point, the people that worked for Bob at the liquor store,
sentences.zh: 后来到了这种地步，那些在酒铺为鲍勃工作的人，

sentences.en: if they saw me coming through the big glass windows, Bob would run in the back.
sentences.zh: 如果他们看到我透过大玻璃窗走过来，鲍勃就会跑进后面。

sentences.en: So he didn't have to see me.
Burt Dubrow was not wrong to be starstruck.
sentences.zh: 伯特·杜布罗被明星吸引并没有错。

sentences.en: It's hard to overstate just how massive a cultural juggernaut Howdy Doody was.
sentences.zh: 很难夸大《豪迪·杜迪》作为一种文化巨头有多么巨大。

sentences.en: The show was disproportionately important to the history of television.
sentences.zh: 该节目在电视史上具有极其重要的地位。

sentences.en: It was the first television program to reach 1,000 episodes,
sentences.zh: 它是第一个达到1000集的电视节目，

sentences.en: one of the first shows to be broadcast in color.
sentences.zh: 也是最早以彩色播出的节目之一。

sentences.en: And it pioneered new ways of marketing products to children.
sentences.zh: 它开创了向儿童推销产品的新方式。

sentences.en: All of which, while I was talking to Burt, begged the question.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，当我和伯特交谈时，都引出了一个问题。

sentences.en: When I was doing the show on Saturday mornings and then running the liquor store the rest of the week,
sentences.zh: 当我在周六早上做节目，然后在剩下的时间里经营酒铺时，

sentences.en: It made sense for him to buy the liquor store.
sentences.zh: 他买下酒铺是有道理的。

sentences.en: If it seems strange that the star of one of the most successful programs on television
sentences.zh: 如果说电视上最成功的节目之一的明星

sentences.en: needed a side hustle, well, today it would be.
sentences.zh: 需要一份副业看起来很奇怪，嗯，放在今天确实会很奇怪。

sentences.en: But in the early days of the medium, especially when Howdy Doody first started,
sentences.zh: 但在电视媒介的早期，尤其是《豪迪·杜迪》刚开始的时候，

sentences.en: the world of television was strange.
It was a place where no one knew what anything or anyone was worth,
sentences.zh: 那是一个没人知道任何东西或任何人价值几何的地方，
连水牛鲍勃自己都不知道。

sentences.en: And honestly, the fact that he ran a liquor store isn't even the strangest part.
sentences.zh: 老实说，他经营酒铺甚至还不是最奇怪的部分。

sentences.en: In many ways, the story of Howdy Doody is the story of the weird Wild West days of early TV.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，《豪迪·杜迪》的故事就是早期电视那段狂野西部时代的故事。

sentences.en: A story in which programmers, advertisers, artists, and money men were inventing everything
sentences.zh: 一个程序员、广告商、艺术家和金主们在边做边发明一切的故事。

sentences.en: Starting with what to put on television in the first place.
sentences.zh: 首先是电视上到底该放什么。

sentences.en: After all, the very first TV shows, including Howdy Doody, had no prior TV shows to build on.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，最早的电视节目，包括《豪迪·杜迪》，都没有先例可循。

sentences.en: Instead, they had to steal their programming ideas from other older mediums, including the
sentences.zh: 相反，他们不得不从其他更古老的媒介中窃取节目创意，包括
所有媒介中最伟大的一个。

sentences.en: Well, it really, you know, Howdy Doody was born on the radio.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它真的，你知道，豪迪·杜迪诞生于广播。

sentences.en: This is music historian Stephen Davis, being interviewed by Terry Gross in 1987.
sentences.zh: 这是音乐历史学家斯蒂芬·戴维斯在1987年接受特里·格罗斯采访时的录音。

sentences.en: His dad worked on Howdy Doody.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲曾在《豪迪·杜迪》工作。

sentences.en: And he says that Buffalo Bob Smith got his name from his hometown of Buffalo, New York.
sentences.zh: 他说“水牛鲍勃”史密斯的名字来源于他的家乡纽约州布法罗市。

sentences.en: And his life in entertainment started early.
sentences.zh: 他的娱乐生涯很早就开始了。

sentences.en: By the time he was four years old, Bob could recreate any melody he heard by plinking away
sentences.zh: 四岁时，鲍勃就能用他那两根小手指在钢琴上弹奏出他听到的任何旋律。

sentences.en: on a piano with his two tiny fingers.
sentences.zh: 四岁时，鲍勃就能用他那两根小手指在钢琴上弹奏出他听到的任何旋律。

sentences.en: And by the time he was in his 30s, he was a popular radio DJ.
sentences.zh: 到了30多岁时，他已经是一位受欢迎的广播DJ了。

sentences.en: He hosted his shows sitting at a piano, where he would sing along to records, perform comedy
sentences.zh: 他坐在钢琴前主持节目，跟着唱片唱歌，表演喜剧小品，

sentences.en: And originally, his sidekick's name was not Howdy Doody.
sentences.zh: 最初，他的搭档名字并不叫豪迪·杜迪。
豪迪最初的名字叫埃尔默。

sentences.en: And he appeared on a Saturday morning quiz show that Buffalo Bob did in those days on
sentences.zh: 他出现在水牛鲍勃当时在NBC广播网做的周六早间问答节目中。
他出现在水牛鲍勃当时在NBC广播网做的周六早间问答节目中。

sentences.en: On the show, Bob developed the persona of Buffalo Bob.
sentences.zh: 在节目中，鲍勃塑造了“水牛鲍勃”的形象。

sentences.en: But he also voiced other characters, including Elmer, who back then was a kind of country bumpkin.
sentences.zh: 但他还为其他角色配音，包括埃尔默，当时他是一个乡巴佬。

sentences.en: And he had this really dumb kind of yokel voice, which kept saying,
sentences.zh: 他有一种非常愚蠢的乡下人口音，一直说，

sentences.en: That was what the Elmer voice sounded like, kind of a rube, a cowboy, you know, somebody
sentences.zh: 这就是埃尔默的声音，有点像个土包子，一个牛仔，你知道，来自边境的人，

sentences.en: from the frontier, a rough dude, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 可以说是一个粗鲁的家伙。

sentences.en: And eventually, that became his name, Howdy Doody.
sentences.zh: 最终，这成了他的名字，豪迪·杜迪。

sentences.en: And in a slightly alternate universe, Howdy would have disappeared from cultural memory
sentences.zh: 在另一个平行宇宙中，当鲍勃的广播节目停播时，豪迪本会从文化记忆中消失。

sentences.en: when Bob's radio program went off the air.
sentences.zh: 但大众媒体，尤其是水牛鲍勃的节目，即将发生巨大的变化，

sentences.en: But mass media, and Buffalo Bob's show in particular, were about to undergo a huge change,
sentences.zh: 这要归功于电视的失败。

sentences.en: thanks to the failure of television.
sentences.zh: 在第一批电视机于30年代商业化之后，很长一段时间里，直到40年代，

sentences.en: After the first television sets became commercially available in the 30s, for a long time, well
sentences.zh: 这种媒介实际上很难流行起来。

sentences.en: into the 40s, the medium actually had a hard time catching on.
sentences.zh: 首先，与拥有各种节目的广播不同，这些小小的、颗粒感十足的黑白屏幕上没什么可看的。

sentences.en: For starters, unlike radio, which had a huge variety of shows, there wasn't much to watch
sentences.zh: 首先，与拥有各种节目的广播不同，这些小小的、颗粒感十足的黑白屏幕上没什么可看的。

sentences.en: on these small, grainy, black-and-white screens.
sentences.zh: 所以，在电视早期，当他们没有太多节目时，

sentences.en: So, in the early days of television, when they didn't have much programming,
sentences.zh: 他们通常的做法就是直接借用当时流行的广播节目，然后将其搬到电视上。

sentences.en: basically what they often did was just borrow the popular radio show of the time and move
sentences.zh: 他们通常的做法就是直接借用当时流行的广播节目，然后将其搬到电视上。
他们通常的做法就是直接借用当时流行的广播节目，然后将其搬到电视上。

sentences.en: I wrote a book about television, and I'm a poet.
sentences.zh: 我写过一本关于电视的书，我还是个诗人。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's what I do.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我的工作。

sentences.en: Did you ever write any poems about Howdy Doody?
sentences.zh: 你写过关于豪迪·杜迪的诗吗？

sentences.en: No, I never wrote a poem about Howdy Doody, nor will I ever.
sentences.zh: 不，我从来没写过关于豪迪·杜迪的诗，以后也不会写。

sentences.en: Stephen says that when televisions first went on the market, few people could afford one.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬说，当电视机刚上市时，很少有人买得起。

sentences.en: In 1948, very few people had televisions.
We're talking fewer than a million people.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是不到一百万人。

sentences.en: And it was not yet a nationwide medium.
sentences.zh: 而且它还不是一种全国性的媒介。

sentences.en: Most of the early television stations were in New York, and those first broadcast signals
sentences.zh: 大多数早期的电视台都在纽约，而那些最初的广播信号传不了那么远。
大多数早期的电视台都在纽约，而那些最初的广播信号传不了那么远。

sentences.en: So, nearly everyone who did own a TV lived in the New York area.
sentences.zh: 所以，几乎所有拥有电视的人都住在纽约地区。

sentences.en: So, what you tended to get in the early days of television were shows that were very New
sentences.zh: 所以，你在电视早期看到的节目往往是非常“纽约”的。

sentences.en: I mean, loud, in your face.
Oh, I couldn't take off your clothes.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不能脱掉你的衣服。
这里有一些奇怪的摄像机。

sentences.en: And the number one television show in the early days of the medium was Milton Berle show,
sentences.zh: 在电视媒介的早期，排名第一的电视节目是《米尔顿·伯尔秀》，

sentences.en: Texaco Star Theater, which was essentially a New York vaudeville show transferred to television.
sentences.zh: 《德士古明星剧场》，这本质上是一个转移到电视上的纽约杂耍表演。

sentences.en: You want to go on television every week?
Yes, but there's one important thing I must tell you, I must tell you, Danny, you've
sentences.zh: 是的，但有一件重要的事情我必须告诉你，我必须告诉你，丹尼，你必须有噱头。

sentences.en: Gimmicks, running gags that you've got to do every week.
sentences.zh: 噱头，就是你每周都得表演的那些老梗。
就像那个苏打水喷人的桥段。
对，就是苏打水那个桥段。

sentences.en: One reason vaudeville worked so well was because of another big hurdle.
sentences.zh: 杂耍表演之所以能如此成功，原因之一在于它克服了另一个巨大的障碍。

sentences.en: Video playback didn't exist yet, meaning television shows in the early days had to go out live.
sentences.zh: 当时还没有视频回放技术，这意味着早期的电视节目必须进行现场直播。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, plenty of shows that worked on the radio, dramas like The Lone Ranger and The
sentences.zh: 与此同时，许多在广播中大获成功的节目，比如《独行侠》和《魅影》这类广播剧，

sentences.en: Shadow, couldn't be adapted for live television, even if they could playback recorded video.
sentences.zh: 即便当时有视频回放技术，也无法改编成电视直播节目。

sentences.en: In the 1940s, no one in the industry was ready to invest those kinds of resources.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪40年代，业内没人准备好投入那种资源。

sentences.en: As a result, there was so little programming being made for television that for a long while,
sentences.zh: 结果，当时制作的电视节目少之又少，以至于很长一段时间里，

sentences.en: there wasn't anything on before dinner time.
sentences.zh: 晚饭前根本没节目可看。

sentences.en: And I don't mean there wasn't anything on like it was boring.
sentences.zh: 我说的不是那种因为无聊而觉得没节目看。

sentences.en: I mean, there was literally nothing on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，电视上真的什么都没有。

sentences.en: The TV networks only broadcast after 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 电视网只在晚上7点以后才播出节目。

sentences.en: But then, in 1947, NBC found something new to put on the air by borrowing a different
sentences.zh: 但到了1947年，NBC（美国全国广播公司）从杂耍表演的剧本中借用了另一招，

sentences.en: Puppets were highly visual, they were live, they were cheap, and perhaps most importantly,
sentences.zh: 木偶戏视觉效果极佳，是现场直播，成本低廉，而且最重要的是，

sentences.zh: 他们的计划是在下午5点这个早得离谱的时间，做一个一小时的儿童特别节目。

sentences.en: They called it Puppet Playhouse, and they tapped Bob Smith to host it, along with his
sentences.zh: 他们将其命名为《木偶剧场》，并邀请鲍勃·史密斯担任主持人，
还有他那乡巴佬搭档——豪迪·杜迪。

sentences.en: And it is important to remember, it didn't have any competition to speak of, because it
sentences.zh: 值得记住的是，它当时几乎没有竞争对手，因为它

sentences.en: was kind of the first network kids show.
sentences.zh: 算是第一个电视网儿童节目。

sentences.en: And just like Milton Berle, it was going to be a vaudeville show made for television.
sentences.zh: 就像米尔顿·伯尔一样，它将是一场为电视制作的杂耍表演。

sentences.en: Howdy Doody, which premiered around the same time on the same network, NBC, was essentially
sentences.zh: 《豪迪·杜迪》几乎在同一时间在同一家电视网NBC首播，本质上

sentences.en: the Milton Berle show for kids.
